audit.why: Early lane favors Lulu (poke/shield range), mid favors Galio (R engage), late favors Lulu again (Wild Growth peel) — content layer already states this correctly.
Power spikes: level 4 Q-E gap close, level 6 R vs single Polymorph, first-item durability grind, two-item Wild Growth peel counter.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..6].side all read the literal string 'Skill' instead of naming which champion wins that stage, contradicting the level chart in win[] and the packet.
audit.why: The chart rule requires full-layer side to name the same side as content win[N]; 'Skill' is not a valid side value and desyncs the visible chart from the prose beneath it.
audit.corrected: Set each phases[N].side to the actual winner (Lulu L1-3, Galio L4-6/first item, Lulu at 2+ items) matching win[0..6], with why rewritten to explain that stage's real interaction (Glitterlance/Pix poke early, Justice Punch gap-close and R at mid, Wild Growth peel late).

edits.before: Q the pair — the tornado tick chips duos that stand in formation.
edits.after: Lulu's Glitterlance-Pix poke out-ranges your engage windup and chips first.

edits.before: W charge threat begins: the taunt governs their engage plans already.
edits.after: Her level-2 poke plus the Help, Pix! shield keep her ahead in every trade.

edits.before: Full kit: E-W the committed trade and the magic shield refunds their poke.
edits.after: Through level 3 Help, Pix!'s shield soaks the autos you'd punish her with.

edits.before: Zone with taunt threat and shield the margins — AP duos pay double rent.
edits.after: Justice Punch (E) finally closes the gap her poke depended on — the swing hits here.

edits.before: Hero's Entrance online — every roam your duo survives, you end.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is an engage her single Whimsy can only half-answer at level 6.

edits.before: First item: the taunt rotation chunks and the MR makes mage supports cry.
edits.after: First-item durability grinds through Help, Pix!'s shield faster than she can reapply it.

edits.before: Late Galio is the anti-dive: taunt their engage off your carry and R the map's emergencies.
edits.after: Two-item Wild Growth plus Whimsy fully peels your lone engage, swinging 2+ items back to her.

edits.before: Bait the answer, start the chain, and let your carry collect — engage trades are all-or-nothing; pick the all.
edits.after: Land E-W the moment Help, Pix! is down — without that shield up, the trade is yours to take and keep.

edits.before: Engaging into a banked disengage — the chain that starts answered is a donation with armor.
edits.after: Charging W into warded brush lets Glitterlance slow the windup and Wild Growth punish the taunt.

edits.before: World Atlas start. Locket or Zeke's line, Mobility-Mercs by lane, then Knight's Vow paths. Add anti-heal early into his duo’s sustain.
edits.after: World Atlas start. Locket or Zeke's line, Mobility-Mercs by lane, then Knight's Vow paths. Add anti-heal early into her duo’s sustain.

edits.before: Commit on Whimsy (Polymorph)’s cooldown, on your first item spike, and with your carry’s damage online. Make him flinch first.
edits.after: Commit on Whimsy (Polymorph)’s cooldown, on your first item spike, and with your carry’s damage online. Make her flinch first.

edits.before: - Lulu Whimsy (Polymorph): matchup-defining — The polymorph deletes a carry’s kit mid-fight — bait it before the real engage. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep W Shield of Durand banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: - Lulu Whimsy (Polymorph): 18s cooldown — it deletes a carry's kit mid-fight for 1.5s; bait it before the real engage. The duo's tempo bends around that timer. - Keep W Shield of Durand banked for their best play. - The R is a fight decision, not a habit.
